rule: Call through a parameter, local variable or stored property holding a function (callback, closure, fn pointer, delegate) → callee is the variable's name, `call_type` callback, confidence unknown. | Not calls: passing a method reference (`x::m`, `self.m` without call), enum-variant/data construction (Rust `Some(x)`, `E::V(..)`, Haskell `Con {..}`), casts, language constructs (`isset`, `empty`, `sizeof`), declarations/function heads, module attributes, typespecs, field access without a call.
notes: check and onDone are delegate parameters; handler is a local holding a method group (not a function literal, so not a named nested function): callback, unknown, callee = variable name. `= Handle` is a method reference without a call: no edge. `as`, the cast (long)n, typeof, nameof, sizeof and default(...) are casts / language constructs: no edge. The lambda `x => x > 0` folds into Wire and makes no call.
